name: Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
description: PCA is a linear dimensionality reduction technique that transforms data to a new coordinate system where the greatest variance lies on the first coordinate (first principal component), the second greatest on the second coordinate, and so on. It finds orthogonal directions of maximum variance in the data.

concept.eigenDecomposition: Find eigenvectors and eigenvalues of covariance matrix
concept.principalComponents: Eigenvectors of covariance matrix, ordered by eigenvalue magnitude
concept.varianceExplanation: Each PC explains a portion of total variance
concept.projection: Map data onto top k principal components
concept.mathematicalFormulation: X' = XW where W contains top k eigenvectors of Σ = (1/n)XᵀX
concept.explanation: PCA finds directions where data varies most. First PC captures maximum variance, second PC captures max variance orthogonal to first, etc.

idealScenarios: Reduce dimensionality before ML (speed/curse of dimensionality)
avoidWhen: When feature interpretability required (features become combinations)

nComponents.impact: If float (0-1), select number to explain that variance proportion

svdSolver.impact: Randomized faster for large data; arpack for few components

whiten.impact: Removes correlations, useful for downstream ML

tol.impact: Components with singular values <= tol removed

preprocessing: Center data (subtract mean) - critical for PCA
Standardize features (optional, recommended if different scales)
Outliers can skew results (consider robust PCA)
determineComponents: Scree plot: variance vs component number
Cumulative variance: find k explaining 90-95% variance
Kaiser criterion: keep components with eigenvalue > 1

complexity.timeTransform: O(k × p) - project to k components
complexity.scalability: Good for moderate dimensions; randomized for large

cons: Components less interpretable than original features

variants.kernelPca: PCA in high-dimensional feature space via kernel trick
